title: Mutual Fund Performance
question: How should a fund's return be judged against its risk?
changed: The reward-to-variability ratio, now the Sharpe ratio: excess return per unit of volatility.

title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
question: How do you get a statistic's sampling distribution without a formula?
changed: The bootstrap: resample the data with replacement and recompute.

title: Using daily stock returns: The case of event studies
question: Do event-study methods work on daily data, with its fat tails and non-synchronous trading?
changed: Simple market-model methods work well by simulation; most refinements add little.

title: Data-Snooping Biases in Tests of Financial Asset Pricing Models
question: What happens to tests when portfolios are sorted on characteristics found in the same data?
changed: Sorting on known return predictors badly inflates test statistics: data snooping, quantified.

title: The Stationary Bootstrap
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
question: How do you bootstrap dependent time series?
changed: Resample blocks of random geometric length, so the resampled series stays stationary.

title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological)
question: With many tests, how do you limit false discoveries without losing all power?
changed: Control the expected share of false discoveries with a simple step-up rule on sorted p-values.

title: Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap
question: Do the best technical trading rules survive accounting for the whole universe searched?
changed: Across about 8,000 rules, the best looked significant in-sample but not after the reality check, and failed later.

title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
question: Is the best of many models really better than the benchmark?
changed: The reality check: bootstrap the maximum performance over all models tried to get an honest p-value.

title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
question: How precisely can a Sharpe ratio be estimated?
changed: Standard errors for the Sharpe ratio, and how autocorrelation distorts annualizing by √12.

title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
question: Can the reality check be made less conservative?
changed: The SPA test: studentize and drop clearly bad models so they don't dilute the test's power.

title: Comparing Sharpe ratios: So where are the p-values?
question: What is the Sharpe ratio's standard error when returns aren't normal?
changed: Asymptotic distributions of Sharpe ratios and their differences that allow skewness, kurtosis and serial dependence.

label: Bailey–López de Prado 2014
title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
question: What is a backtest's Sharpe ratio worth after trying many variants?
changed: The deflated Sharpe ratio: test against the expected maximum Sharpe of N trials, adjusted for skew and kurtosis.

title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
question: What happens to anomalies after they are published?
changed: Anomaly returns are about 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication: data mining explains some of the decay, investors learning the rest.

title: … and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
question: With hundreds of published factors, what t-statistic should count as a discovery?
changed: Multiple-testing corrections across the factor zoo: a new factor needs t above about 3, and many published ones are likely false.

title: The probability of backtest overfitting
question: How likely is it that the best in-sample configuration underperforms out of sample?
changed: Combinatorially symmetric cross-validation estimates the probability of backtest overfitting directly.

title: Presidential Address: The Scientific Outlook in Financial Economics
question: Why do so many published findings fail, and what should change?
changed: Incentives favor significant results; proposed Bayesianized p-values and higher standards of evidence.

title: Replicating Anomalies
question: How many of 452 published anomalies survive careful replication?
changed: Controlling microcaps with NYSE breakpoints and value weights, most anomalies lose significance.

title: Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing
question: Can the anomaly literature be reproduced from open code?
changed: Open-source code for over 300 predictors; nearly all clearly significant originals reproduce.

title: Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?
question: Do factors replicate once evidence is pooled properly?
changed: A Bayesian model across 153 factors and 93 countries: most factors replicate, and the zoo collapses into a few themes.
